page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6v-c8g1.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance powered by KVM virtualization. The instance features an Intel Xeon 8163 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at 2.5 GHz. The host CPU includes 33 MB of L3 cache alongside AES, BMI2, and ADX instructions, though modern vector extensions such as AVX, AVX-512, and AMX are disabled or absent. Memory capacity is configured at 128.0 GB of RAM, equating to 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by 4 NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs totaling 64 GB of VRAM (16 GB per GPU). The instance includes a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, 0 complimentary public IPv4 addresses, and no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions.

Benchmark results demonstrate intermediate multi-core and memory capabilities alongside constrained single-thread performance. The stress-ng multi-core CPU benchmark achieved 23,575.63 points (middle 50%), and the PassMark CPU score registered at 21,092.78 points. PassMark subtests yielded 9,124.26 for extended instructions, 10,928.19 for encryption, and 2,504.70 for physics calculations. Conversely, single-thread performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core scoring 1,103.89 (bottom 25%), single-threaded gzip compression recording 19.1 GB/sec (bottom 10%), and single-threaded bzip3 decompression achieving 7.53 GB/sec (bottom 25%). Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression recovered to 112.53 GB/sec. Memory subsystem benchmarks show 1,313.7 GB/sec for small-block cached reads, 118.4 GB/sec for large uncached reads, and 57.05 GB/sec for large writes, complemented by a PassMark memory score of 1,887.73. Application-level metrics show standard throughput, producing 22.1 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 15.55 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

From a cost-efficiency and architecture standpoint, this instance trades host CPU single-thread potency for high-density multi-GPU compute. The lack of built-in local NVMe disks requires off-instance storage, introducing potential I/O latency considerations for disk-heavy pipelines. Furthermore, the absence of host AVX and AVX-512 capabilities shifts vector and tensor calculation requirements entirely onto the NVIDIA V100 accelerators. The server is suited for multi-GPU training, distributed deep learning inference, high-performance parallel computing, and GPU-accelerated scientific simulations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6v-c8g1.8xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance featuring 32 vCPUs (16 physical cores at 2.5 GHz) via an Intel Xeon 8163 processor and 128.0 GB of RAM. The instance incorporates 4 NVIDIA Volta V100 GPUs with 64 GB total VRAM, a 10 Gbps baseline network interface, and no local storage. Benchmark results show average multi-core CPU performance with a stress-ng score of 23,575.63 and PassMark CPU score of 21,092.78, but weaker single-thread throughput, highlighted by a single-core stress-ng score of 1,103.89 and gzip compression of 19.1 GB/sec. System memory throughput reaches 118.4 GB/sec for large-block reads and 57.05 GB/sec for writes. With host vector instruction sets absent, the system relies on its quad-GPU architecture for parallel compute workloads such as deep learning training, model inference, and scientific simulations.
